decisions.reason: Explains that ordinary unary failures resolve with ok:false/error and never enter catch, while the current code treats resolution as success; correctly notes the RemoteResult shape predates alpha.2 (exists since rc.2). Grounds the diagnosis in the fixture's result.ok/result.value expressions, which unambiguously identify the renameSession body.

Identifies four distinct, explained defects anchored in fixture expressions: reading result.value unchecked, misusing catch as the business-failure path, cross-realm instanceof RemoteError, and converting genuine rejects into a retry loop.
The fenced ts block awaits the remote call, branches on !result.ok, handles result.error and returns before ever reading result.value — correct discriminated control flow.
States success as ok:true/value, ordinary failure as ok:false/error, and that catch is not on the ordinary failure route; no code-renaming distraction.

Correctly scopes genuine rejects to assembly/programming faults with concrete examples (wrong arity, unmounted method, missing Context adapter) and requires propagation/exposure rather than swallowing or retrying; does not conflate business failures with these faults.

Rejects instanceof across bundles/workers/realms, requires structural code-based discrimination on the failed result, and confines isRemoteFailure to a genuine thrown boundary rather than replacing the result discriminant check.

caps.reason: The report affirmatively states ordinary failures resolve with ok:false and do not enter catch — the opposite of the misconception.
The proposed fix discriminates on result.ok before reading value, uses no instanceof, and contains no retry or swallowing of genuine rejects.
